{{external media | width = 180px | float = right | headerimage= [[File:Pregabalin 3-isobutyl GABA.png|180px]] | video1 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qGRoEG8xiZU "Richard B. Silverman, Basic Science to Blockbuster Drug"], [[National Academy of Inventors]]}}

'''Richard Bruce Silverman''' (born May 12, 1946) is the Patrick G. Ryan/Aon Professor of [[Chemistry]] at [[Northwestern University]]. His group's main focus is basic and translational research into central nervous system disorders and cancer. He is known for the discovery of [[pregabalin]], which is marketed by [[Pfizer]] under the brand name Lyrica.<ref name=Lyrica>{{cite news | first=Theo | last=Francis | title=Health Blog: Lyrica Makes Rain at Northwestern | date=August 17, 2007 | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/BL-HEB-927 | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | access-date = April 17, 2008 }}</ref>

==Education==
Silverman attended [[Central High School (Philadelphia)|Central High School of Philadelphia]].<ref name="Alumni">{{cite news|title=Dedication of the Silverman Faculty Lounge|url=http://centralhighalumni.com/admin/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/CHS-Alumni-Journal-Spring-2014.pdf|access-date=May 20, 2016|work=The Alumni Journal|agency=Central High School of Philadelphia|date=2014|archive-date=June 17, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617073340/http://centralhighalumni.com/admin/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/CHS-Alumni-Journal-Spring-2014.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Silverman received his B.S. in chemistry from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1968. He spent one semester at [[Harvard University]] before being drafted and serving as a [[United States Army]] Physical Sciences Assistant at the [[Walter Reed Army Institute of Research]] from January 1969 until his honorable discharge in January 1971. In June 1974, he received his Ph.D. from Harvard University in [[organic chemistry]] with advisor [[David Dolphin]]. He then spent two years as a postdoctoral fellow with Robert Abeles in biochemistry at [[Brandeis University]].<ref name=CV/>

==Research==
Silverman has been teaching and doing research at Northwestern since 1976. He became both professor of chemistry and professor of biochemistry, molecular biology, and cell biology in 1986. He has held several named professorships. He was the Arthur Andersen Professor of Chemistry from 1988 to 1996, the Charles Deering McCormick Professor of Teaching Excellence from 2001 to 2003,<ref name="IBIO"/> and the John Evans Professor of Chemistry beginning from 2004 to 2015.<ref name="MEDI">{{cite web|title=Richard B. Silverman, Ph.D.|url=https://www.acsmedchem.org/?nd=Silverman|website=ACS Division of Medicinal Chemistry|access-date=May 19, 2016}}</ref> He was named the inaugural Patrick G. Ryan/Aon Professor as of September 1, 2015.<ref name=CV>{{cite web |url=http://chemgroups.northwestern.edu/silverman/resume.htm |title=Curriculum Vitae |access-date=April 17, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080515164351/http://chemgroups.northwestern.edu/silverman/resume.htm |archive-date=May 15, 2008 }}</ref>

The primary focus in Silverman's laboratory is basic research into [[Central nervous system disease|central nervous system disorders]], including [[Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis]] (ALS), [[Parkinson's disease]], [[Alzheimer's disease]], and [[epilepsy]].<ref name="Merrill"/> Other research areas include cancer ([[melanoma]] and [[hepatocellular carcinoma]]). He has developed novel approaches to the elucidation of enzyme-catalyzed reactions in organic chemistry.<ref name="Wessner"/> He is interested in understanding and developing mechanisms of [[enzyme inhibition]].<ref name="Purich">{{cite book|chapter=Mechanism-based enzyme inactivators|last=Silverman|first=Richard B. |editor-last1=Purich|editor-first1=Daniel L.|title=Contemporary enzyme kinetics and mechanism|date=2009|publisher=Elsevier/Academic Press|location=Amsterdam|isbn=9780123847447|pages=331–|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Pr3V80HZLpkC&pg=PA331}}</ref>

Silverman has published about 400 research articles. He has been awarded 130 patents. He has written 3 books (one in the third edition): ''Mechanism-Based Enzyme Inactivation: Chemistry and Enzymology'' (CRC Press; 1988), ''Organic Chemistry of Drug Design and Drug Action'' (Academic Press; 1992, 2004, 2014), and ''Organic Chemistry of Enzyme-Catalyzed Reactions'' (Academic Press; 2000, 2002; see the Published works section, below). He is active on the editorial boards of a number of scholarly journals.<ref name="Wessner" />

Silverman is known for inventing the drug pregabalin as a possible treatment for [[epileptic seizures]].<ref name="Merrill"/> During 1988-1990, Ryszard Andruszkiewicz, a visiting research fellow, synthesized a series of molecules for Silverman.<ref name="Andruszkiewicz">{{cite journal|last1=Andruszkiewicz|first1=R|last2=Silverman|first2=RB|title=4-Amino-3-alkylbutanoic acids as substrates for gamma-aminobutyric acid aminotransferase.|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|date=December 25, 1990|volume=265|issue=36|pages=22288–91|doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(18)45702-X|pmid=2266125|doi-access=free}}</ref> One looked promising.<ref name="Poros"/> The molecule was transported into the brain, where it activated the enzyme L-glutamate decarboxylase. Silverman anticipated that the enzyme would increase production of the inhibitory neurotransmitter [[GABA]] and block convulsions.<ref name="Merrill"/> Eventually, the set of molecules were sent to Parke-Davis Pharmaceuticals for testing. In addition to treating seizures, pregabalin was found to be effective in treating [[fibromyalgia]] pain, [[neuropathic pain]], and [[generalized anxiety disorder]].<ref name="Merrill"/> It was approved by the FDA in 2004 and marketed by [[Pfizer]] (which bought Parke-Davis) under the trade name Lyrica.<ref name="Merrill">{{cite news|last1=Merrill|first1=Nick|title=Silverman's golden drug makes him NU's golden ticket|url=http://www.northbynorthwestern.com/story/silvermans-golden-drug-makes-him-nus-golden-ticket/|access-date=May 19, 2016|work=North by Northwestern|date=February 25, 2010|archive-date=June 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601194802/http://www.northbynorthwestern.com/story/silvermans-golden-drug-makes-him-nus-golden-ticket/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Poros">{{cite news|last1=Poros|first1=Joanna|title=Polish scientist is the co-author of a new anti-epileptic drug|url=http://scienceinpoland.pap.pl/en/news/news,16089,polish-scientist-is-the-co-author-of-a-new-anti-epileptic-drug.html|access-date=May 19, 2016|work=Science and Scholarship in Poland|date=2005|archive-date=August 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820094019/http://scienceinpoland.pap.pl/en/news/news,16089,polish-scientist-is-the-co-author-of-a-new-anti-epileptic-drug.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Research has shown that the mechanism of the drug is more complicated than originally anticipated.<ref name="Silverman">{{cite journal|last1=Silverman|first1=Richard B.|title=From Basic Science to Blockbuster Drug: The Discovery of Lyrica|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|date=April 28, 2008|volume=47|issue=19|pages=3500–3504|doi=10.1002/anie.200704280|pmid=18307181}}</ref> In addition to its effects on GABA-AT substrate behavior, pregabalin binds to calcium channels and blocks glutamate release. GABA is potentiated, but through a different mechanism than originally suspected.<ref name="Taylor">{{cite journal|last1=Taylor|first1=CP|last2=Angelotti|first2=T|last3=Fauman|first3=E|title=Pharmacology and mechanism of action of pregabalin: the calcium channel alpha2-delta (alpha2-delta) subunit as a target for antiepileptic drug discovery.|journal=Epilepsy Research|date=February 2007|volume=73|issue=2|pages=137–50|pmid=17126531|doi=10.1016/j.eplepsyres.2006.09.008|s2cid=54254671}}</ref><ref name="Lowe">{{cite web|last1=Lowe|first1=Derek|title=Getting To Lyrica|url=https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/getting-lyrica|website=Science Translational Medicine|date=March 25, 2008}}</ref>

===Teaching awards===
Silverman has received numerous teaching awards from Northwestern University, including the following:
* 1999 E. LeRoy Hall Award for Teaching Excellence
* 1999 Excellence in Chemistry Education Award from the Northwestern University chapter of [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] Chemistry Fraternity
* 2000 Alumni Association Excellence in Teaching Award
* 2001-2004 Charles Deering McCormick Professor of Teaching Excellence

==Philanthropy==
Lyrica royalties paid to Northwestern, and a gift from Silverman himself, have supported the Silverman Hall for Molecular Therapeutics and Diagnostics at Northwestern University. Silverman Hall, which opened in 2009, was designed to be a collaborative and interdisciplinary facility housing researchers from chemistry, biology, and engineering.<ref name="Merrill"/><ref name="Thornton">{{cite web|title=Northwestern University Richard and Barbara Silverman Hall for Molecular Therapeutics and Diagnostics|url=http://www.thorntontomasetti.com/projects/northwestern_university_richard_and_barbara_silverman_hall_for_molecular_therapeutics_and_diagnostics/|website=Thornton Tomasetti|access-date=May 19, 2016|archive-date=November 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107025523/http://www.thorntontomasetti.com/projects/northwestern_university_richard_and_barbara_silverman_hall_for_molecular_therapeutics_and_diagnostics/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
